{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_d9122d5c5b1c4610806d7d30","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Normalized Event Schema\n2\t\n3\t## Overview\n4\t\n5\tThe normalized event schema is the harness-agnostic contract between event producers (adapters, detectors) and the Trail Boss daemon. All normalized events are submitted to the `/event/normalized` endpoint and share a common structure with a `type` discriminator.\n6\t\n7\tThis design isolates harness coupling to the adapter layer — the daemon consumes only normalized events and has no knowledge of harness-specific formats (Claude Code hooks, tmux detector, etc.).\n8\t\n9\t## Type Discriminator\n10\t\n11\tAll normalized events have a required `type` field that serves as a discriminated union discriminator:\n12\t\n13\t```typescript\n14\ttype NormalizedEvent = StuckEvent | UnstuckEvent | SessionRegistered | SessionEnded;\n15\t```\n16\t\n17\tType guards are used to narrow the type at runtime:\n18\t\n19\t```typescript\n20\tfunction isStuckEvent(event: unknown): event is StuckEvent {\n21\t  return (event as NormalizedEvent)?.type === \"stuck\";\n22\t}\n23\t```\n24\t\n25\t## Event Types\n26\t\n27\t### 1. StuckEvent\n28\t\n29\tA session became stuck and needs attention. This is the core event that adds a session to the queue.\n30\t\n31\t```typescript\n32\tinterface StuckEvent {\n33\t  type: \"stuck\";\n34\t  sessionId: string;\n35\t  paneId: string;\n36\t  cwd: string;\n37\t  transcriptPath: string;\n38\t  reason: \"stopped\" | \"permission\";\n39\t  message: string;\n40\t  timestamp: number; // Unix milliseconds\n41\t}\n42\t```\n43\t\n44\t**Required Fields:**\n45\t\n46\t| Field | Type | Validation |\n47\t|-------|------|------------|\n48\t| `type` | `\"stuck\"` | Must be exactly `\"stuck\"` |\n49\t| `sessionId` | `string` | Non-empty, unique identifier for the session |\n50\t| `paneId` | `string` | tmux pane ID (e.g., `%446`) or synthetic equivalent |\n51\t| `cwd` | `string` | Current working directory (empty string if unknown) |\n52\t| `transcriptPath` | `string` | Absolute path to transcript JSONL (empty string if unknown) |\n53\t| `reason` | `\"stopped\" \\| \"permission\"` | Must be exactly `\"stopped\"` or `\"permission\"` |\n54\t| `message` | `string` | Context message (e.g., last assistant message, tool name) |\n55\t| `timestamp` | `number` | Unix milliseconds, must be > 0 |\n56\t\n57\t**Field Semantics:**\n58\t\n59\t- `sessionId`: Unique identifier for the session. For Claude Code, this is the harness session ID. For tmux detector, this is synthetic: `tmux-{paneId}-{timestamp}`.\n60\t- `paneId`: tmux pane identifier (e.g., `%446`). Used for navigation to the stuck session.\n61\t- `cwd`: Working directory for context display. May be empty for synthetic sessions.\n62\t- `transcriptPath`: Path to the session's transcript JSONL for reconciliation. May be empty for synthetic sessions (tmux detector has no transcript).\n63\t- `reason`: Why the session is stuck. `\"stopped\"` = session hit a Stop hook. `\"permission\"` = session is waiting at a permission prompt. Tmux detector always uses `\"stopped\"` (cannot distinguish).\n64\t- `message`: Human-readable context. For stopped sessions, this is the last assistant message. For permission sessions, this is the tool name and input. For tmux detector, this is the last line of output.\n65\t- `timestamp`: When the stuck event occurred. All normalized events are submitted to the `/event/normalized` endpoint and share a common structure with a `type` discriminator.\n\nThis design isolates harness coupling to the adapter layer — the daemon consumes only normalized events and has no knowledge of harness-specific formats (Claude Code hooks, tmux detector, etc.).\n\n## Type Discriminator\n\nAll normalized events have a required `type` field that serves as a discriminated union discriminator:\n\n```typescript\ntype NormalizedEvent = StuckEvent | UnstuckEvent | SessionRegistered | SessionEnded;\n```\n\nType guards are used to narrow the type at runtime:\n\n```typescript\nfunction isStuckEvent(event: unknown): event is StuckEvent {\n  return (event as NormalizedEvent)?.type === \"stuck\";\n}\n```\n\n## Event Types\n\n### 1. StuckEvent\n\nA session became stuck and needs attention. This is the core event that adds a session to the queue.\n\n```typescript\ninterface StuckEvent {\n  type: \"stuck\";\n  sessionId: string;\n  paneId: string;\n  cwd: string;\n  transcriptPath: string;\n  reason: \"stopped\" | \"permission\";\n  message: string;\n  timestamp: number; // Unix milliseconds\n}\n```\n\n**Required Fields:**\n\n| Field | Type | Validation |\n|-------|------|------------|\n| `type` | `\"stuck\"` | Must be exactly `\"stuck\"` |\n| `sessionId` | `string` | Non-empty, unique identifier for the session |\n| `paneId` | `string` | tmux pane ID (e.g., `%446`) or synthetic equivalent |\n| `cwd` | `string` | Current working directory (empty string if unknown) |\n| `transcriptPath` | `string` | Absolute path to transcript JSONL (empty string if unknown) |\n| `reason` | `\"stopped\" \\| \"permission\"` | Must be exactly `\"stopped\"` or `\"permission\"` |\n| `message` | `string` | Context message (e.g., last assistant message, tool name) |\n| `timestamp` | `number` | Unix milliseconds, must be > 0 |\n\n**Field Semantics:**\n\n- `sessionId`: Unique identifier for the session. For Claude Code, this is the harness session ID. For tmux detector, this is synthetic: `tmux-{paneId}-{timestamp}`.\n- `paneId`: tmux pane identifier (e.g., `%446`). Used for navigation to the stuck session.\n- `cwd`: Working directory for context display. May be empty for synthetic sessions.\n- `transcriptPath`: Path to the session's transcript JSONL for reconciliation. May be empty for synthetic sessions (tmux detector has no transcript).\n- `reason`: Why the session is stuck. `\"stopped\"` = session hit a Stop hook. `\"permission\"` = session is waiting at a permission prompt. Tmux detector always uses `\"stopped\"` (cannot distinguish).\n- `message`: Human-readable context. For stopped sessions, this is the last assistant message. For permission sessions, this is the tool name and input. For tmux detector, this is the last line of output.\n- `timestamp`: When the stuck event occurred. Used for queue ordering and staleness detection.\n\n**Examples:**\n\n```typescript\n// From Claude Code hooks (stopped)\n{\n  type: \"stuck\",\n  sessionId: \"claude-42-abc123\",\n  paneId: \"%446\",\n  cwd: \"/home/coding/project\",\n  transcriptPath: \"/home/coding/.claude/sessions/abc123/transcript.jsonl\",\n  reason: \"stopped\",\n  message: \"The user has not responded. Waiting for input.\",\n  timestamp: 1735689600000\n}\n\n// From Claude Code hooks (permission)\n{\n  type: \"stuck\",\n  sessionId: \"claude-42-def456\",\n  paneId: \"%447\",\n  cwd: \"/home/coding/project\",\n  transcriptPath: \"/home/coding/.claude/sessions/def456/transcript.jsonl\",\n  reason: \"permission\",\n  message: \"Tool: Bash | Command: npm install\",\n  timestamp: 1735689605000\n}\n\n// From tmux detector\n{\n  type: \"stuck\",\n  sessionId: \"tmux-%446-1735689600000\",\n  paneId: \"%446\",\n  cwd: \"/home/coding/project\",\n  transcriptPath: \"\",\n  reason: \"stopped\",\n  message: \"Quiet at prompt: $ \",\n  timestamp: 1735689600000\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2. Decisions & rationale\n\n## Naming\n\n**Trail Boss** — on a cattle drive, the trail boss is in overall command: sets the direction,\nmakes the calls, and rides in when a steer bogs down or strays. The product runs a *herd* of\nagent sessions; when one gets stuck it reports in, and you — the trail boss — ride over and set\nit right. The metaphor maps cleanly onto the mechanism:\n\n- **the herd grazing the range** → sessions working autonomously\n- **a steer bogs down or strays** → a `Stop` / `PermissionRequest` hook fires; the collector\n  flags the session stuck\n- **the trail boss rides over and sets it right** → you read the context and give the order\n  (reply) or wave it on (skip); the queue surfaces stuck sessions oldest-first (flat FIFO, no\n  priority ranking)\n\n### Names considered and rejected\n\n- **`agent-inbox`** — clearest literal description, but collides head-on with\n  [`langchain-ai/agent-inbox`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/agent-inbox), an existing\n  human-in-the-loop inbox for LangGraph agents. Would read as derivative and lose every search.\n- **`agent-attention`** — names the value prop (your attention is the scarce resource being\n  routed), but risks reading as the ML \"attention\" mechanism.\n- **`agent-central`** — self-explanatory but generic, and \"central\" reads like a passive\n  dashboard/hub rather than an act-on-the-stuck-one tool.\n\nTrail Boss keeps a memorable, distinctive identity; the tagline carries the legibility for\nnewcomers.\n\n## Design decisions\n\n### Normalized event API endpoint (2026-07-02)\n\n**Decision:** Add a dedicated `/event/normalized` endpoint that accepts pre-normalized stuck/unstuck events.\n\n**Rationale:**\n\nThe daemon architecture separates detection (harness-coupled) from the core queue logic (harness-agnostic). To maintain this separation, we need a normalized event contract that isolates harness coupling to the adapter layer.\n\nTwo approaches were considered:\n\n1. **New normalized endpoint** (`/event/normalized`): Accepts pre-normalized events with a `type` field. Harness-specific adapters (Claude Code hooks, tmux detector) emit normalized events directly.\n2. **Server-side adapter wrapper**: Keep single `/event` endpoint, register multiple server-side adapters that wrap different event formats in a common Claude hook format.\n\n**Option 1 was chosen** for these reasons:\n\n- **Clean separation**: The adapter lives at the emission site (hook script or detector), not in the daemon. The daemon consumes only normalized events and has no knowledge of harness-specific formats.\n- **Protocol simplicity**: A single `type` field enables discriminated unions and type guards. The daemon implementation may currently only support the legacy `/event` endpoint; see Implementation Status below.\n\n## HTTP Request\n\n### Endpoint\n\n**URL:** `http://127.0.0.1:4000/event/normalized`\n\n**Method:** `POST`\n\n**Headers:**\n```\nContent-Type: application/json\n```\n\n**Configuration:** The daemon URL is configurable via `TRAILBOSS_DAEMON_URL` environment variable (default: `http://127.0.0.1:4000/event/normalized`)\n\n## Event Payloads\n\nThe tmux detector emits four event types, each with a specific structure:\n\n### 1. Registered Event\n\nEmitted when a pane with `@tb-` prefix is discovered.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"registered\",\n  \"sessionId\": \"tmux-%446-1735689600000\",\n  \"paneId\": \"%446\",\n  \"cwd\": \"/home/coding/trail-boss\",\n  \"transcriptPath\": \"\",\n  \"timestamp\": 1735689600000\n}\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- `sessionId` is synthetic: `tmux-{paneId}-{timestamp}`\n- `transcriptPath` is always empty (tmux detector has no transcript file)\n- `cwd` is obtained via `tmux display -p -t {paneId} '#{pane_current_path}'`\n\n### 2. Stuck Event\n\nEmitted when pane is quiet for 30s and last line looks like a prompt.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"stuck\",\n  \"sessionId\": \"tmux-%446-1735689600000\",\n  \"paneId\": \"%446\",\n  \"cwd\": \"/home/coding/trail-boss\",\n  \"transcriptPath\": \"\",\n  \"reason\": \"stopped\",\n  \"message\": \"Quiet at prompt: $ \",\n  \"timestamp\": 1735689600000\n}\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- `reason` is always `\"stopped\"` (tmux detector cannot distinguish permission blocks)\n- `message` is the last line of pane output (for context display)\n- Triggered when: `now - lastOutputTime >= QUIET_THRESHOLD_MS` AND `looksLikePrompt(output)`\n\n### 3. Unstuck Event\n\nEmitted when pane output changes after being stuck.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"unstuck\",\n  \"sessionId\": \"tmux-%446-1735689600000\",\n  \"timestamp\": 1735689660000\n}\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- Emitted when output hash changes while `isStuck == true`\n- Only `sessionId` and `timestamp` required\n\n### 4.
